## 2. Description of the Service

Privytics is an independent, managed, EU-hosted product-analytics platform. It enables you to collect, store, and analyse usage and behavioural data about the end-users of your own websites and applications.

Key characteristics of the Service:

- **Cookieless by design.** The Service does not set cookies and does not use device storage on your end-users' devices for its core anonymous analytics. Anonymous visitor identification uses a daily-rotating, salted hash derived from IP address, user agent, and project identifier; the salt rotates every midnight UTC, so anonymous identifiers reset daily.
- **Identified analytics** occur only when you explicitly call the `identify()` method with your own user identifier and optional traits (such as name or email). That data is personal data that you control and are responsible for.
- **Session replay** is available on paid plans, is opt-in per project, and masks all text and inputs by default (rrweb-based). It is switched off on the free tier.
- **Consent gating** is available: you can initialise the SDK in a disabled state (`disabled: true`) and call `ready()` once you have obtained any consent you require.
- **AI features.** Where available, paid plans can use an optional AI assistant (chat, report drafting, a natural-language filter and insight explanations), subject to daily usage limits. On all plans, weekly digest emails may include a short AI-written summary. AI features rely on the third-party AI providers listed in our Privacy Policy, and the data they use is sent to those providers as described there.

Privytics is built on the open-source **OpenPanel** analytics engine, licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0). Privytics is an independent product and is **not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by OpenPanel** (https://openpanel.dev).

# Privytics Privacy Policy

**Last updated: 17 November 2026**

Privytics is an independent, EU-hosted, managed product-analytics service operated at [privytics.com](https://privytics.com). This Privacy Policy explains what personal data we process, why we process it, the legal bases we rely on, who we share it with, and the rights you have. It applies to visitors to our website, holders of Privytics accounts, and the individuals whose data we process on behalf of our customers.

We have written this policy to be honest and specific. Where personal data leaves the European Economic Area (EEA), or where a third party is involved, we say so plainly rather than making blanket promises we cannot keep.

---

## 1. Who We Are and How to Contact Us

Privytics is a product-analytics platform built on the open-source OpenPanel analytics engine (AGPL-3.0, [openpanel.dev](https://openpanel.dev)). Privytics is an independent service and is **not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by OpenPanel**. The corresponding source code for the version of OpenPanel that Privytics runs is published, in accordance with the AGPL-3.0 licence, at [github.com/sergiarguimbau/privytics](https://github.com/sergiarguimbau/privytics).

The data controller responsible for the personal data described in this policy (except where we act as a processor, see Section 3) is:

- **Legal entity:** Sergi Arguimbau Guarinos (NIF ES43221590J)
- **Registered address:** Carrer Isaac Newton, Edifici Disset, 3a planta, D-1, Parc Bit, 07120 Palma de Mallorca, Spain
- **Country of establishment:** Spain
- **Phone:** +34 669 62 91 69
- **Email:** [hello@privytics.com](mailto:hello@privytics.com)

If you have any question about this policy or wish to exercise your rights, please contact us at [hello@privytics.com](mailto:hello@privytics.com).

---

## 2. A Note on Our Own Analytics: We Are Cookieless

Privytics is a privacy-first analytics product, and we apply the same principles to our own website and dashboard. Our analytics are **cookieless**:

- We set **no cookies** and use **no local storage, session storage, device fingerprinting persistence, or any other on-device identifier**.
- Instead of tracking an individual across visits, an anonymous "device id" is derived as a **daily-rotating salted hash of the visitor's IP address, user agent, and project id**. The salt rotates every midnight UTC, so these identifiers **reset every day** and, for visitors who are not signed in, cannot be used to follow a person over time.
- The personal data processed to produce anonymous analytics (the hashed IP address and user agent) is **minimal and transient**, and is not retained in raw form.

**When you are signed in to the dashboard** (app.privytics.com), we also use Privytics to understand how account holders use it, so we can improve onboarding and the product and help you when you contact us. While you are signed in, the pages you view and the actions you take (for example creating a project, building a report or inviting a teammate) are linked to your account: your user id, email address and name, with the approximate location (country, region and city) and device and browser type derived from each request. If you sign up or sign in during the same visit as a visit to privytics.com, the pages you viewed there and how you arrived are linked to your account too. This uses the same cookieless technique, so nothing is stored on your device for it. It never includes the data of our customers' end users: dashboard page addresses are recorded without their query string and with the identifiers of profiles, sessions, groups, AI traces, share links and invitations removed; links you follow to other sites are recorded by their domain only; and nothing you type into forms or dialogs is sent. Embeddable widgets and public share links send nothing. Only the Privytics team can see this usage data. It is stored in our own Privytics project in the EU (Germany) and kept as described in Section 8; if we use the AI features described in Section 4.2 on that project, the data they look up is sent to the AI providers listed in Section 7. You can object at any time by writing to [hello@privytics.com](mailto:hello@privytics.com).

Because we do not store information on your device or set cookies for analytics, our own use of Privytics analytics, on the website and in the dashboard, **does not require a cookie consent banner**. This same design is what our customers use when they deploy Privytics on their own websites and apps (see Section 3).

---

## 3. Our Two Roles: Controller and Processor

It is important to understand that Privytics wears two different hats depending on the data in question.

### 3.1 Where we are the Controller

For the following, **Privytics is the data controller** and this Privacy Policy governs our processing:

- Personal data of **visitors to privytics.com** (see Section 2 on our cookieless analytics).
- **Account data** of the people who sign up for and administer a Privytics account.
- **Billing data** relating to your subscription (processed through our Merchant of Record, see Section 6).
- **Support correspondence** you send to us.

### 3.2 Where we are the Processor

When a customer uses Privytics to collect analytics about **that customer's own end-users** (for example, the visitors to the customer's website or the users of the customer's app), the **customer is the controller** of that data and **Privytics acts as the processor**, processing it only on the customer's documented instructions.

That processor relationship is governed by our **Data Processing Agreement (DPA)**, which forms part of our Terms of Service and sets out the subject matter, duration, nature and purpose of the processing, the categories of data subjects and personal data, and the security and sub-processing commitments we make. If you are an end-user of one of our customers and have questions about how your data is used, please contact **that customer** as the controller. Our customers can request a copy of the DPA at [hello@privytics.com](mailto:hello@privytics.com).

---

## 4. Categories of People and Data We Process

| Category of people | Data we process | Our role |
|---|---|---|
| Website visitors (privytics.com) | Transient hashed IP + user agent (daily-rotating salted hash), pages viewed, referrer, approximate location (country, region and city), device/browser type; linked to your account if you sign up or sign in during the same visit (see Section 2) | Controller |
| Account holders | Name, email address, hashed password or federated login identifier, organisation name, project configuration, login and audit metadata, the messages you send to the AI assistant, and how you use the dashboard while signed in (pages viewed and actions taken, with approximate location and device/browser type, see Section 2) | Controller |
| Billing contacts | Subscription plan, billing email, billing address/country, VAT status, transaction and invoice records (card data is handled by the payment processor, not stored by us) | Controller (billing operated by Polar as Merchant of Record) |
| People who contact support | Email address, message content, and any information you choose to include | Controller |
| Our customers' end-users | Cookieless anonymous analytics events; and, only where the customer calls `identify()`, the customer's own user id plus optional traits such as name and email; optional session-replay recordings (masked by default); optional AI observability traces the customer sends about its own AI features (prompts, responses, tool calls, and model, token and cost data); and any of this data that the AI assistant looks up to answer a question (see Section 4.2) | Processor (customer is controller) |

### 4.1 Analytics data in more detail (processor context)

- **Anonymous analytics** rely on the daily-rotating salted hash described in Section 2. No cookies or device storage are used.
- **Identified analytics** occur **only when the customer chooses to call `identify()`** with their own user identifier and, optionally, traits such as name or email. This is personal data that the **customer controls** and instructs us to process.
- **Session replay** is **opt-in per project** and **off by default** (including always off on the free tier). It is built on rrweb and **masks all text and input fields by default**.
- Privytics offers **built-in consent gating** for customers who need it, allowing the SDK to start in a disabled state (`disabled: true`) and only begin processing once the customer signals consent by calling `ready()`.

### 4.2 AI features

Privytics includes AI features that use the APIs of **OpenAI** and, only where OpenAI is not configured, **Anthropic**, under our own accounts with those providers:

- **AI assistant (paid plans only).** The chat assistant, report drafting, the natural-language filter on the overview page, and explanations of insights run only when a signed-in user on a paid plan asks for them. For each request we send the provider the user's message (in the chat, together with the earlier messages of the same conversation), the project's name and timezone, and the data the assistant looks up to answer. Depending on the question, that data can include end-users' personal data held in the project, such as a profile's user id, name, email and traits, and individual events with their properties, page paths, device details and approximate location (city level), as well as your organisation's plan and usage, your Search Console data, and the email of a teammate you ask it to invite. Conversations are saved in the account so users can return to them. What you type is account data, for which we are the controller; end-user data the assistant looks up and saves in a conversation is processed for the customer, as its processor.
- **Insight summaries.** Once a day, for projects with an active subscription and enough traffic, we send the traffic changes Privytics detected automatically (aggregated figures by page path, referrer, country or device type, without profile ids, names or emails; page paths and referrers are sent as recorded, so any personal data in your URLs is included) to OpenAI to rank them and write short summaries.
- **Weekly digest summary (all plans, including free).** Each week, for projects with traffic, OpenAI writes a short paragraph for the weekly summary email from the project's name, its weekly totals and up to five notable insights. No profile ids, names or emails are sent for this, but the insights can name page paths and referrers as recorded.

Under their business API terms, OpenAI and Anthropic do not use this data to train their models. They keep API inputs and outputs for up to 30 days for abuse and safety monitoring, and longer where required by law or to investigate misuse (for Anthropic, up to two years for content flagged for a usage-policy violation). OpenAI also stores each request and response for 30 days by default, so that later requests in a conversation can refer to them. Both providers contract with us through their Irish entities, but AI requests are processed outside the EU, including in the US, under Standard Contractual Clauses (see Section 7).

---

## 5. Purposes and Legal Bases

We rely on the following legal bases under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and equivalent laws:

- **Performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b)):** to create and administer your account, provide the analytics service, process your subscription, and provide support.
- **Legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f)):** to operate, secure, debug, and improve our service; to prevent fraud and abuse (for example bot protection); to understand usage of our own website via cookieless analytics, and how signed-in account holders use the dashboard, so we can improve onboarding and the product and support you; and to communicate service-related information. Where we rely on legitimate interests, we balance those interests against your rights and freedoms, and you may object (see Section 9).
- **Legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c)):** to comply with tax, accounting, and other legal requirements, including retaining invoicing records.
- **Consent (Art. 6(1)(a)):** where we ask for it, for example optional product communications. You may withdraw consent at any time without affecting processing carried out before withdrawal.

When we act as a **processor** for customer analytics data (Section 3.2), the **customer** is responsible for establishing the appropriate legal basis for the processing they instruct us to perform.

---

## 6. Billing and Payments

Payments are handled by **Polar** ([polar.sh](https://polar.sh)), which acts as the **Merchant of Record** and **seller of record** for Privytics subscriptions. This means:

- **Polar processes your payment** and uses **Stripe** as its underlying payment processor.
- **Polar collects and remits EU VAT** as the seller of record.
- Privytics does not receive or store your full card number; that information is handled by Polar and Stripe under their own privacy terms and PCI-DSS obligations.

Our plans include a **free tier** (10,000 events/month, no card required, 12-month data retention, one project, community support, session replay off) and **paid stepped tiers** (€10/100k, €20/500k, €40/1M, €100/5M, €200/10M events per month, and custom pricing above 10M), which add session replay and longer retention. **All prices exclude VAT**, which is applied and remitted by Polar.

---

## 7. Sub-Processors and International Transfers

We use a small number of carefully selected sub-processors to run the service. Some of them are established in the **United States**. We do **not** claim that "no data leaves the EU": while all **analytics event data is stored in the EU** (Germany), certain **operational functions involve providers that are US companies**, in some cases even where the data itself is held in the EU. This covers payments, email, error monitoring, website and dashboard hosting, our account database, and the AI features described in Section 4.2.

For every sub-processor located outside the EEA, transfers are carried out under the European Commission's **Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs)**, together with appropriate supplementary and technical measures. For OpenAI and Anthropic, whose contracting entities are in Ireland, onward transfers to their US group companies are covered by the Standard Contractual Clauses in each provider's data processing terms (for OpenAI, SCCs or an adequacy decision).

| Sub-processor | Purpose | Region |
|---|---|---|
| EU data-centre provider | Hosting of analytics event data and encrypted backups | Germany / EU |
| Neon Inc. | Managed PostgreSQL for account, organisation, and project data, including saved AI assistant conversations | Germany / EU (AWS eu-central-1); US company |
| Polar Software Inc. | Payments and Merchant of Record (uses Stripe as its processor) | US |
| Resend | Delivery of transactional and service emails, including alerts and weekly analytics digests | US (AWS us-east-1) |
| Sentry | Application error monitoring | US or EU region |
| Better Stack | Uptime monitoring and public status page | EU / US |
| Cloudflare | Website and dashboard hosting, delivery of the `op1.js` tracking script, bot protection (Turnstile), and R2 backup storage | US / global |
| OpenAI Ireland Ltd (US group company: OpenAI OpCo, LLC) | AI features: assistant answers, report drafts, filters, insight summaries and explanations, and weekly digest paragraphs | US / global (contracting entity in Ireland) |
| Anthropic Ireland, Limited (US group company: Anthropic, PBC) | AI assistant, used only where OpenAI is not configured | US / global (contracting entity in Ireland) |

Because payments (Polar/Stripe), email (Resend), error monitoring (Sentry), and the AI features (OpenAI, Anthropic) may involve processing in the US, personal data such as your billing details, email address, diagnostic information, messages you send to the AI assistant, or analytics data it looks up (which can include end-users' personal data) may be transferred to the US under SCCs. A current list of sub-processors is available on request at [hello@privytics.com](mailto:hello@privytics.com); we will give customers notice of material changes as set out in our DPA.

---

## 8. Data Retention

We keep personal data only for as long as necessary for the purposes described in this policy:

- **Analytics event data (processor):** retained according to the customer's plan: **12 months** on the free tier and **5 years** on any paid plan. Customers may delete projects and data earlier.
- **AI observability traces (processor):** prompt, response and tool-call content is deleted automatically after about **30 days**; the rest of each trace (model, token, cost and timing data, error messages, custom properties and linked ids) follows the plan retention above.
- **AI assistant conversations (controller for your messages; processor for end-user data they contain):** kept in the account until a user deletes the conversation or the user, project or organisation is deleted. They can contain analytics data, including end-user personal data, that the assistant looked up.
- **Account data (controller):** retained for as long as your account is active, and for a reasonable period afterwards to handle wind-down, disputes, and legal obligations, after which it is deleted or anonymised.
- **Dashboard usage analytics (controller):** your profile in our own Privytics project (user id, email address, name, approximate location and device type) is kept while your account exists and deleted when you close it. The pages viewed and actions taken are kept for up to **5 years**, the retention of that project; once your account is closed they are no longer linked to your name or email. You can ask us to delete them sooner at any time.
- **Billing and invoicing records:** retained for the period required by applicable tax and accounting law.
- **Support correspondence:** retained for as long as needed to resolve your matter and for a reasonable period thereafter.
- **Backups:** regular encrypted, off-site backups are retained on a rolling basis and are overwritten or expired in the ordinary course; data deleted from live systems persists in backups only until those backups age out.

---

## 9. Your Rights

Subject to the conditions and exemptions in applicable law, you have the right to:

- **Access** the personal data we hold about you;
- **Rectification** of inaccurate or incomplete data;
- **Erasure** of your data ("right to be forgotten");
- **Restriction** of processing in certain circumstances;
- **Data portability**, to receive your data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format;
- **Object** to processing based on our legitimate interests;
- **Withdraw consent** at any time where processing is based on consent.

To exercise any of these rights in relation to data for which **we are the controller**, contact us at [hello@privytics.com](mailto:hello@privytics.com). We will respond within the timeframes required by law.

If you are an **end-user of one of our customers**, the customer is the controller of that data; please direct your request to them. We will assist our customers in responding to such requests as required by our DPA.

You also have the right to **lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority**, in particular in the EU Member State of your habitual residence, place of work, or the place of the alleged infringement. We would, however, appreciate the chance to address your concerns first.

---

## 10. Consumer Right of Withdrawal (EU B2C)

If you are a consumer in the EU purchasing a paid digital service, you generally have a **14-day right of withdrawal**. Because our paid plans provide **immediate access** to a digital service, we ask, at checkout, for your **express consent to begin performance immediately** and your **acknowledgment that you lose the right of withdrawal once the service has been fully performed**. This consent and acknowledgment are confirmed to you on a **durable medium**. Where performance has begun with your consent but is not yet complete, any withdrawal will be handled in accordance with applicable consumer law.

---

## 11. Security

We take the protection of personal data seriously and maintain technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risk, including:

- **Encryption in transit** using TLS;
- **Encryption at rest** for stored data;
- **Access controls** and the principle of least privilege for our systems;
- An **isolated ClickHouse** analytics store;
- **Regular encrypted, off-site backups**;
- Documented **breach detection and response procedures**, including notification to authorities and affected individuals where required by law.

No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, but we work continuously to protect your data and to improve our safeguards.

---

## 12. Children

Privytics is a business-to-business analytics service and is **not directed to children**. We do not knowingly collect personal data directly from children. Where our customers use Privytics on their own properties, it is the customer's responsibility, as controller, to ensure their use complies with applicable laws concerning minors.

---

## 13. International Users

Privytics is operated from the EU and analytics event data is hosted in Germany. If you access our service from outside the EEA, please be aware that your data may be processed in the EEA and, for the operational functions described in Section 7, in the United States, in each case with appropriate safeguards such as SCCs. By using the service, you understand that your data will be handled as described in this policy.

---

## 14. Changes to This Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time to reflect changes to our service, our sub-processors, or legal requirements. When we make material changes, we will update the "Last updated" date above and, where appropriate, notify account holders by email or through the dashboard. We encourage you to review this policy periodically.

---

## 15. Contact

If you have any questions, requests, or concerns about this Privacy Policy or your personal data, please contact us at:

**[hello@privytics.com](mailto:hello@privytics.com)**

---

*This document is provided for general information and should be reviewed by qualified legal counsel for your applicable jurisdiction before being relied upon.*

# Data Processing Agreement

This Data Processing Agreement ("DPA") forms part of, and is incorporated by reference into, the Privytics Terms of Service (the "Agreement") between the customer identified in the Agreement (the "Customer") and Sergi Arguimbau Guarinos (NIF ES43221590J), a sole trader (autónomo) established in Spain with registered address at Carrer Isaac Newton, Edifici Disset, 3a planta, D-1, Parc Bit, 07120 Palma de Mallorca, Spain ("Privytics"). 1.3. This DPA does not apply to Personal Data for which Privytics acts as an independent controller, including Personal Data relating to visitors to privytics.com and Personal Data relating to the Customer's own account, billing, and support interactions. Privytics' Processing of that data as a controller is described in the Privytics Privacy Policy.

---

## 2. Definitions

Capitalised terms not defined in this DPA have the meaning given to them in the Agreement or the GDPR. In this DPA:

- **"Applicable Data Protection Law"** means all laws and regulations applicable to the Processing of Personal Data under the Agreement, including the GDPR, the GDPR as retained in the law of the United Kingdom, and any implementing or supplementing national laws.
- **"Controller"** means the natural or legal person which, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the Processing of Personal Data.
- **"Processor"** means the natural or legal person which Processes Personal Data on behalf of the Controller.
- **"Personal Data"** means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person that is Processed by Privytics on behalf of the Customer under the Agreement.
- **"Processing"** (and "Process") means any operation performed on Personal Data, whether or not by automated means, such as collection, recording, storage, use, disclosure, or erasure.
- **"Data Subject"** means the identified or identifiable natural person to whom Personal Data relates.
- **"Sub-processor"** means any third party engaged by Privytics to Process Customer Personal Data.
- **"Personal Data Breach"** means a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, Customer Personal Data.
- **"Standard Contractual Clauses"** or **"SCCs"** means the standard contractual clauses for the transfer of personal data to third countries adopted by the European Commission under Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914, and, where relevant, the UK International Data Transfer Addendum.
- **"EEA"** means the European Economic Area.
- **"Supervisory Authority"** means an independent public authority established under the GDPR.

---

## 3. Subject Matter and Details of Processing

3.1. The subject matter, duration, nature and purpose of the Processing, the categories of Data Subjects, and the categories of Personal Data are set out in **Annex I** and are incorporated into this DPA by reference.

3.2. Privytics shall Process Customer Personal Data only for the purpose of providing and supporting the service under the Agreement and in accordance with the Customer's documented instructions.

---

## 4. Processor Obligations

Privytics shall comply with the obligations of a processor under Article 28(3) of the GDPR. In particular, Privytics shall:

### 4.1. Documented Instructions

(a) Process Customer Personal Data only on the documented instructions of the Customer, including with regard to transfers of Personal Data to a third country, unless required to do otherwise by EU or Member State law to which Privytics is subject; in that case Privytics shall inform the Customer of that legal requirement before Processing, unless the law prohibits such information on important grounds of public interest.

(b) Treat the Agreement, this DPA (including its Annexes), and the ordinary use and configuration of the service by the Customer as the Customer's complete and final documented instructions. Additional or alternative instructions must be agreed in writing.

(c) Inform the Customer without undue delay if, in Privytics' opinion, an instruction infringes Applicable Data Protection Law. Privytics is not obliged to carry out a legal review of the lawfulness of the Customer's instructions.

### 4.2. Confidentiality

Privytics shall ensure that persons authorised to Process Customer Personal Data have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality, and that access is limited to personnel who need it to perform the Agreement.

### 4.3. Security

Privytics shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, in accordance with Article 32 of the GDPR. (a) assist the Customer, by appropriate technical and organisational measures and insofar as possible, in fulfilling the Customer's obligation to respond to requests from Data Subjects exercising their rights under Chapter III of the GDPR (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, and objection). ---

## Annex I — Details of the Processing

**Subject matter.** The provision of the Privytics managed product-analytics service to the Customer under the Agreement, including ingestion, storage, aggregation, and presentation of analytics data.

**Nature and purpose of the Processing.** Collection and receipt of analytics events transmitted by the Customer's applications or websites via the Privytics SDKs and ingestion endpoint (api.privytics.com); computation of anonymous, daily-rotating device identifiers; storage of event and, where enabled, session-replay data; aggregation and querying to produce analytics dashboards, reports, and insights presented in the Privytics app (app.privytics.com) and in emails to the Customer's account users (team members), such as alerts and weekly digests; AI-assisted analysis, in which the relevant analytics data, which may include Customer Personal Data, is sent to the AI providers listed in Annex III to generate assistant answers, report drafts, filters, insight summaries and explanations, and weekly digest paragraphs, with the resulting assistant conversations stored in the Customer's account; storage of AI observability traces the Customer sends about its own AI features; and related support.

Prompt, response and tool-call content is deleted after about 30 days, and the Customer can turn off its storage per project. |

**Special categories of Personal Data.** None are intended or required. The Customer must not transmit special-category data (Article 9 GDPR) to the service except where it has a lawful basis and has configured masking and consent appropriately.

**Frequency of the Processing.** Continuous, for the duration of the Agreement.

---

## Annex II — Technical and Organisational Measures

Privytics implements and maintains the following technical and organisational measures pursuant to Article 32 of the GDPR:

- **Encryption at rest.** Stored analytics data and backups are encrypted at rest.

- **Backups and restore.** Regular encrypted, off-site backups are taken, with restore procedures tested periodically.

- **Breach response.** Documented procedures for detecting, investigating, escalating, and notifying Personal Data Breaches, including a single point of contact.
- **Vendor management.** Sub-processors are assessed for data protection and security, and bound by written contracts with appropriate safeguards, including the Standard Contractual Clauses where relevant.

# Cookie Policy

**Last updated: 17 November 2026**

Privytics is an independent, managed, EU-hosted product-analytics service operated by Sergi Arguimbau Guarinos (NIF ES43221590J), registered at Carrer Isaac Newton, Edifici Disset, 3a planta, D-1, Parc Bit, 07120 Palma de Mallorca, Spain ("Privytics", "we", "us", "our"). This Cookie Policy explains how cookies and similar technologies are used across the Privytics analytics product, our website at privytics.com, and our dashboard application at app.privytics.com.

The short version: our analytics product is cookieless and sets nothing on your visitors' devices. Our own website and dashboard use a small number of strictly necessary cookies to keep you logged in and to keep the service secure, plus a few preference cookies that remember dashboard settings such as your theme. We do not use advertising or cross-site tracking cookies anywhere, and our own product analytics, on the website and in the dashboard, sets no cookies either.

## What are cookies and similar technologies?

Cookies are small text files that a website stores in your browser. They are commonly used to remember sign-in state, preferences, or to track people across websites. "Similar technologies" include local storage, session storage, and other forms of on-device storage that can be used for comparable purposes.

Under EU law (the ePrivacy Directive and national implementations), storing or reading information on a user's device generally requires consent, unless the storage is strictly necessary to provide a service the user has explicitly requested. This is why many websites show a cookie banner. It is also why, as explained below, a website using the Privytics analytics product does not need a cookie banner on account of Privytics.

## The Privytics analytics product is cookieless

When you embed Privytics analytics on your website or in your application, Privytics does **not**:

- set any cookies on your visitors' devices;
- read any existing cookies from your visitors' devices;
- use local storage, session storage, IndexedDB, fingerprinting, or any other form of device or browser storage to identify or track visitors; or
- persist any identifier on the visitor's device across sessions.

### How we count visitors without cookies

Instead of storing an identifier on the device, Privytics derives an anonymous, non-persistent "device id" on the server. This id is a salted hash computed from:

- the visitor's IP address,
- the visitor's user agent, and
- the project id of the site collecting the data.

The salt rotates every midnight UTC. Because the salt changes daily, the derived ids reset every day and cannot be correlated across days. The IP address and user agent are processed transiently to compute this hash and are not stored as raw identifiers for anonymous analytics. The result is a privacy-preserving, day-scoped count that requires nothing to be written to or read from the visitor's device.

### What this means for cookie banners

Because Privytics analytics stores and reads nothing on the visitor's device by default, the consent requirement for cookies and similar device storage does not apply to Privytics analytics. As a result, a website using Privytics generally does **not** need to include Privytics in a cookie consent banner.

The one exception is optional: if a site calls the SDK's `pendingRevenue()` helper, the revenue amounts it records are kept in that browser tab's session storage until the next page sends them. This holds no identifier and is cleared once sent. Sites that use this helper should assess it under their own cookie and device-storage obligations.

Please note two things:

- This statement concerns cookies and device-storage consent only. Your own website may still require a cookie banner because of other tools you use, and you remain responsible for assessing your overall obligations. Separately, your processing of any personal data through Privytics is governed by data-protection law and by our Data Processing Agreement; this Cookie Policy does not address those obligations.
- **Identify and session replay features.** If you call our `identify()` function, you send us a user id and optional traits (such as name or email) that you control; this is not achieved through cookies, but it is personal data you are responsible for. If you enable **session replay** for a project, Privytics records on-page interactions (with all text and inputs masked by default). Session replay is not a cookie and does not rely on cookies, but it does capture behavioural data, so you should account for it in your own privacy notices and, where appropriate, obtain consent from your users. Privytics also offers built-in consent gating (initialising with `disabled: true` and later calling `ready()`) so you can hold off on any collection until your user has consented.

## Cookies used on privytics.com and app.privytics.com

While the analytics product is cookieless, our own website and dashboard do use a small number of **strictly necessary** cookies, and a few **preference** cookies. The strictly necessary cookies are required to provide the service you have explicitly requested (for example, logging in and keeping your session secure) and, under EU law, do not require consent.

We use these cookies for:

- **Authentication and session management** — keeping you signed in to your account and dashboard.
- **Security** — protecting sign-in and forms against automated abuse, including via Cloudflare Turnstile (a privacy-respecting, no-cookie-by-default bot-protection challenge that may in some cases set a strictly necessary security token).
- **Preferences**: remembering choices you make in the dashboard, such as your theme, your date range and your last sign-in method.

We do **not** use:

- advertising or marketing cookies;
- cross-site or third-party tracking cookies;
- analytics cookies (we use our own cookieless product to understand usage of our site and dashboard); or
- social-media or ad-network pixels.

### Strictly necessary cookies (illustrative)

The exact cookie names and lifetimes may change as we improve the service. The following table is illustrative of the strictly necessary cookies we use:

| Cookie name | Purpose | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| `openpanel.session_token` | Maintains your authenticated login session on app.privytics.com | Up to 30 days, renewed while you use the dashboard |
| `openpanel.state` | Protects Google or GitHub sign-in against forged requests | 5 minutes, only during that sign-in |
| `openpanel.two_factor` | Keeps a two-factor sign-in challenge pending | 10 minutes, only during that sign-in |
| `inviteId` | Remembers the team invitation you are accepting while you sign in | 10 minutes |
| `gsc_oauth_state`, `gsc_code_verifier`, `gsc_project_id` | Secure the Google Search Console connection and remember which project it is for | 10 minutes, only while connecting Search Console |
| `cf_challenge` (illustrative) | Set by Cloudflare Turnstile to complete a bot-protection challenge when required | Short-lived (minutes) |

These are first-party, strictly necessary cookies. We do not sell or share the information they contain, and they are not used for profiling or advertising.

### Preference cookies

These first-party cookies remember choices you make in the dashboard. They are not used for tracking, profiling or advertising.

| Cookie name | Purpose | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-theme` | Remembers the colour theme you chose for the dashboard | Up to 10 years |
| `range` | Remembers the date range you last selected | Up to 10 years |
| `feedback-prompt-seen` | Remembers that you have seen the feedback prompt, so it is not shown again | 30 days |
| `last-auth-provider` | Remembers which sign-in method you last used, so the sign-in page can point to it | 1 year |

The dashboard also keeps similar display preferences, such as table column choices and dismissed banners, in your browser's local storage on app.privytics.com. These are not used for tracking either.

## Managing and controlling cookies

Disabling our strictly necessary cookies may prevent you from signing in or using the dashboard; disabling preference cookies only means the dashboard forgets your settings. You can still control cookies through your browser at any time:

- **Delete cookies** already stored by your browser.
- **Block cookies** entirely or on a per-site basis.
- **Receive a warning** before a cookie is stored.

Most browsers let you manage these settings under their privacy or security preferences. For guidance, see the help pages for your browser (for example, Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge). If you block strictly necessary cookies for app.privytics.com, core features such as logging in will not work.

## Changes to this Cookie Policy

We may update this Cookie Policy from time to time to reflect changes in the technologies we use or in applicable law. When we make material changes, we will update the "Last updated" date at the top of this page.

## Contact us

If you have questions about this Cookie Policy or our use of cookies, contact us at **hello@privytics.com**.

---

*This document is provided for general informational purposes and does not constitute legal advice. It should be reviewed by qualified legal counsel for the applicable jurisdiction before being relied upon.*

# Getting Started with Privytics

Privytics is a managed, EU-hosted, cookieless product analytics platform. This guide walks you through creating a project, installing the SDK, and sending your first events. It takes about five minutes.

- App and dashboard: `https://app.privytics.com`
- Ingestion API: `https://api.privytics.com`

## 1. Create a project and get your client id

1. Create a free account at [app.privytics.com/onboarding](https://app.privytics.com/onboarding), or sign in at [app.privytics.com](https://app.privytics.com) if you already have one.
2. Sign-up asks you to create your first project (for example, "My Website" or "Production App"). The free plan includes one project; paid plans can add more.
3. Open **Project settings → Clients** and copy your **Client ID**.

Your client id is a public identifier used to route incoming events to your project. Throughout this guide it is shown as `YOUR_CLIENT_ID`.

## 2. Install the SDK

You can install Privytics with a simple script tag or with the npm package. Both use the same OpenPanel Web SDK under the hood.

### Option A: Script tag

Drop this into the `<head>` of your HTML. It loads the SDK, initializes it with your credentials, and enables automatic screen view and outgoing link tracking.

```html
<script>
  window.op =
    window.op ||
    function (...args) {
      (window.op.q = window.op.q || []).push(args);
    };
  window.op('init', {
    apiUrl: 'https://api.privytics.com',
    clientId: 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID',
    trackScreenViews: true,
    trackOutgoingLinks: true,
  });
</script>
<script src="https://privytics.com/op1.js" defer></script>
```

### Option B: npm package

Privytics runs the open-source OpenPanel engine, so it uses OpenPanel's open-source SDKs. Install `@openpanel/web` (OpenPanel's package, published under the `@openpanel` npm scope) and point `apiUrl` at Privytics so all data reports to your Privytics project. Privytics is an independent service and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by OpenPanel.

```bash
npm install @openpanel/web
```

```ts
import { OpenPanel } from '@openpanel/web';

export const op = new OpenPanel({
  apiUrl: 'https://api.privytics.com',
  clientId: 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID',
  trackScreenViews: true,
  trackOutgoingLinks: true,
});
```

### Option C: framework packages (Next.js, React, and more)

The framework packages are OpenPanel's, published under the `@openpanel` scope, so some defaults point at OpenPanel's infrastructure. One setting you must change, and one you may want to:

| Setting | Required? | Set it to | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apiUrl` | **Required** | `https://api.privytics.com` | Without it the SDK posts your events to `api.openpanel.dev`, so your data lands in OpenPanel's service rather than your Privytics project |
| `scriptUrl` | Optional | `https://privytics.com/op1.js` | The component injects a `<script>` tag that defaults to `openpanel.dev/op1.js`. The integration works fine either way. Set it if you would rather serve the tracker from a domain you control, so your visitors' browsers do not make a request to a third party |

Next.js:

```bash
npm install @openpanel/nextjs
```

```tsx
import { OpenPanelComponent } from '@openpanel/nextjs';

export function Analytics() {
  return (
    <OpenPanelComponent
      apiUrl="https://api.privytics.com"
      scriptUrl="https://privytics.com/op1.js"
      clientId="YOUR_CLIENT_ID"
      trackScreenViews
      trackOutgoingLinks
    />
  );
}
```

`scriptUrl` only applies to framework components, because they inject the `<script>` tag for you. Option A does not need it (you write the `src` yourself) and Option B does not need it either (your bundler resolves the SDK, including the session-replay recorder, so nothing is fetched from a CDN). OpenPanel's own self-hosting guide keeps their CDN default and changes only `apiUrl`, so treat `scriptUrl` as a first-party-delivery preference rather than a correctness fix.

The one thing to carry over from their examples is `apiUrl`: everything else in the [SDK guides](https://openpanel.dev/docs) applies to you unchanged, and section 7 has the full list.

## 3. Track custom events

Track any meaningful action with a name and optional properties.

```ts
op.track('signup_completed', {
  plan: 'pro',
  referrer: 'newsletter',
});

op.track('button_clicked', {
  label: 'Start free trial',
});
```

Event names should be human readable and consistent (`checkout_started`, `video_played`). Properties can be strings, numbers, or booleans.

## 4. Identify users

By default, Privytics is fully anonymous and cookieless. When you know who a user is, call `identify()` to attach your own user id and optional traits.

```ts
op.identify({
  profileId: 'user_12345',
  email: 'jane@example.com',
  firstName: 'Jane',
  lastName: 'Doe',
  properties: {
    plan: 'pro',
  },
});
```

### Anonymous vs identified

- **Anonymous analytics (default, cookieless):** No cookies and no device storage are used. An anonymous device id is derived from a daily-rotating salted hash of IP address, user agent, and project id. The salt rotates every midnight UTC, so anonymous ids reset daily. This keeps the data minimal and transient.
- **Identified analytics:** When you call `identify()`, events are linked to the `profileId` you provide (your own user id). This is data you control. Use `identify()` only after you have the appropriate legal basis or consent to associate analytics with a known individual.

To clear the identity, for example on logout:

```ts
op.clear();
```

## 5. Session replay

Session replay is a paid-plan feature. On the free plan the API does not accept recordings, so turning it on there records nothing. It is off by default and starts only when you enable it in your tracking code. It is built on rrweb and **masks all text and inputs by default**, so sensitive content is not captured unless you explicitly unmask it. Recordings are kept for 30 days on every plan.

To turn it on, initialize the SDK with `sessionReplay: { enabled: true }`:

```ts
export const op = new OpenPanel({
  apiUrl: 'https://api.privytics.com',
  clientId: 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID',
  trackScreenViews: true,
  trackOutgoingLinks: true,
  sessionReplay: {
    enabled: true,
  },
});
```

With the script tag (Option A), add the same `sessionReplay` block to the `window.op('init', { ... })` call. The recorder then loads on demand from `https://privytics.com/op1-replay.js`. The snippet under **Project settings → Tracking script** in the dashboard already includes this block, commented out.

Masking is controlled by `maskAllText` and `maskAllInputs` (both on by default) and `unmaskTextSelector`. Review them before enabling replay in production.

## 6. Consent gating

If you need to wait for user consent before any data is sent, start the SDK in a disabled state and call `ready()` once consent is granted.

```ts
export const op = new OpenPanel({
  apiUrl: 'https://api.privytics.com',
  clientId: 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID',
  trackScreenViews: true,
  trackOutgoingLinks: true,
  disabled: true, // no events are sent yet
});

// Later, after the user accepts analytics:
op.ready();
```

While `disabled` is `true`, no events leave the browser. Calling `ready()` flushes queued events and resumes normal tracking.

## 7. Supported SDKs and REST API

Privytics works with OpenPanel's SDKs. Point each one at `https://api.privytics.com` with your client id. OpenPanel publishes seven official JavaScript packages, and one of them covers several frameworks:

- **Script tag, plain JavaScript, React, Vue and Remix:** `@openpanel/web`
- **Next.js:** `@openpanel/nextjs`
- **Nuxt:** `@openpanel/nuxt`
- **Astro:** `@openpanel/astro`
- **React Native:** `@openpanel/react-native`
- **Express:** `@openpanel/express`
- **Node and other JavaScript runtimes:** `@openpanel/sdk`

For Swift, Kotlin, Python, Ruby, Rust and Java there are SDKs outside the `@openpanel` npm scope, some of them community-maintained. Each one has a [setup guide](/for) that says how it installs.

Prefer to integrate directly? Send events to the Privytics **REST API** at `https://api.privytics.com` using your client id. This is ideal for server-side tracking or languages without a dedicated SDK.

## 8. Open source and deeper references

Privytics is powered by the open-source **OpenPanel** analytics engine. Privytics is an independent managed service and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by OpenPanel.

Because the SDKs are shared, the OpenPanel documentation is an excellent deep reference for advanced configuration and per-framework guides. One value in their examples is theirs, not yours: set `apiUrl` to `https://api.privytics.com` so your data reaches Privytics. Optionally set `scriptUrl` too, if you would rather serve the tracker from your own domain than from OpenPanel's CDN. See Option C in section 2.

- SDK references and advanced guides: [https://openpanel.dev/docs](https://openpanel.dev/docs)

## Need help?

Reach out any time at [hello@privytics.com](mailto:hello@privytics.com). Happy tracking.
